items.title: Cookie
items.summary:
A playful challenge where your identity is determined by a cookie. Can you prove to the server that you are the true Cookie Monster?
TL;DR Cookie is a web security challenge that demonstrates the risks of unverified, client-controlled cookies. The server sets an initial cookie user=anonymous and checks if the cookie value matches cookie_monster. Because cookies are completely under client control and lack digital signatures (such as HMAC), modifying the cookie header to user=cookie_monster grants unauthorized access and leaks the flag. items.title: Basic Injection
items.summary:
See if you can leak the whole database using what you know about SQL Injections.
TL;DR Basic Injection is a fundamental web exploitation challenge demonstrating classic SQL Injection. The backend query incorporates user input directly via string concatenation without parameterization. Submitting a tautology payload (' OR 1=1 -- -) forces the SQL statement to evaluate to true for every record in the table, dumping the entire database contents and revealing the flag.
